query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Microalloying single-phase fcc FeCoNi with a few atomic percent boron will introduce boride precipitates and grain-boundary segregation that pin domain walls, boosting coercivity to the few-hundred oersted range while retaining high saturation magnetization.
generation.material_initial_state: Polycrystalline single-phase fcc Fe50Co25Ni25 (grain size ~1–50 µm, Hc ≈50 Oe, Ms ≈1.45 T at 300 K).
generation.intervention: Add 3 at.% B into the FeCoNi melt prior to casting.
generation.conditions: Arc‐melt under Ar, suction-cast into rods, melt-spin ribbons at 30 m/s; anneal at 600 °C for 1 h in Ar, cool at 10 °C/min; measure magnetic hysteresis by VSM at 300 K up to 1.5 T.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of nanometer-scale boride precipitates segregated to grain boundaries and concomitant grain refinement to ≲100 nm.
generation.mechanism: Grain-boundary boride phases act as strong pinning centers for domain walls, raising effective magnetocrystalline anisotropy and thus Hc.
generation.predicted_outcome: Coercivity increases to ~200–300 Oe (3–6× baseline) while Ms remains within 90% of original (≳1.3 T).
generation.baseline: Hc ≈50 Oe, Ms ≈1.45 T for undoped Fe50Co25Ni25 measured under identical conditions.
generation.boundary: FeCoNi matrix composition ±5 at.%, B content 1–5 at.%, grain size 50–200 nm, 300 K measurement, max field 1.5 T.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate—exact Hc gain depends on B content, heat treatment, and final grain size; Ms loss uncertain within ±0.1 T.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two alloy sets: Fe50Co25Ni25 and Fe47Co24Ni24B3 under identical synthesis and annealing; characterize grain size and boride phase distribution by TEM/EDX and XRD; record full hysteresis loops by VSM at 300 K up to 1.5 T.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the B-doped alloy fails to show ≥50% increase in Hc (i.e. Hc <75 Oe) or if no boride phases are detected at grain boundaries, the hypothesis is falsified.
